project.name: M2.11 rehearsal - Beyond the Horizon
project.brief: Sample target website, not Studio chrome or a real commissioned exhibition. Create an online exhibition companion contrasting observed space photography with imagined space travel. Visitors should browse two entries, read their credits and context, and distinguish a documentary photograph from speculative illustration.
project.audience: Curious non-experts viewing on a phone or desktop; no design or astronomy vocabulary required.
project.purpose: Let each artwork feel distinctive while keeping the catalogue and entry reading experience coherent.
project.constraints: Real source content: Earthrise, Bill Anders/NASA, 24 December 1968; The Grand Tour, Invisible Creature, NASA/JPL-Caltech Visions of the Future. Two routes: catalogue and entry detail. Credits adjacent to each image; readable mobile captions; no copy embedded in images; preserve source image proportions. All references are inspiration only. No assets, direction, fonts or motion are approved. No fabricated exhibition opening date or ticket availability. Rehearsal choices do not establish a permanent user taste profile.

frames.name: C - Quiet / graphic rhythm
frames.concept: Mixed direction: quiet surroundings punctuated by graphic-heavy sections and occasional glitch-like moments
frames.feeling: Contrast, atmosphere, breathing room, graphic intensity in selected moments
frames.decisions: Human preference: a mix across separate sections, with quiet surroundings/ending and some graphic-heavy moments. Agent interpretation: this supersedes choosing a uniform A-only or B-only treatment. Episodic glitch is an intentional expressive option, not a blanket anti-slop defect. No immutable approval or specific implementation is selected.
frames.questions: Where should graphic/glitch interruptions occur: section transitions, deliberate interaction, or occasional ambient moments? Which specific reference clip/timestamps should inform timing? What reduced-motion or static alternative preserves the contrast?

annotations.body:
AGENT PROPOSAL A - QUIET EXHIBITION

Borrow: Earthrise's scale contrast and breathing room. Let one complete artwork lead each entry, with readable captions and a short story. Catalogue uses varied image proportions rather than repeated hero banners.

Leave behind: copying the photograph's black field into every page or treating every work as a space backdrop.

Tradeoff: gives art and reading room, but feels less immediately graphic than B. Keep one strong display title if useful; do not shrink navigation or captions to get that effect.

Status: proposal only. No user choice recorded.
Question: should the catalogue feel primarily contemplative or energetic?

annotations.body:
AGENT PROPOSAL B - GRAPHIC CATALOGUE

Borrow: Grand Tour's layered shapes, strong title and repeated directional rhythm. Translate this into chapter markers and a distinctive catalogue header; keep credits and entry reading calm.

Leave behind: tracing the poster layout, forcing its full palette into controls, or moving every horizontal line. Static artwork does not establish a motion recipe.

Tradeoff: more recognisable graphic identity, but dense overlays could compete with the artwork or wrap poorly on phones.

Early critique: a generic dark space hero plus glowing gradient cards would flatten both sources into a familiar template. Compare source-specific scale or graphic rhythm instead. Dark backgrounds remain an option if chosen for a reason.

Status: proposal only. No user choice recorded.

annotations.body: Agent interpretation of the human correction: replace the either-A-or-B framing with contrast across sections and moments. Preserve the two reference-derived ingredient proposals 03233e7d-6d09-428e-ae5d-d686e8e09eab and 627b9132-bfd6-4cc0-bb3b-c621467206e3. Superseded alternative: applying A-only or B-only uniformly across the whole site; that would omit either the requested graphic intensity or quiet surroundings/ending. This rejection is the agent's explicit interpretation of the request for a mix, not an invented verbatim user statement that either style is bad.
annotations.translation: Quiet and graphic coexist with different roles
annotations.limitations: Human preference is recorded; implementation details and any approval remain open.

decision.rationale: The human asked for a mix across separate sections, quiet ending/surroundings, and occasional glitch-like graphic moments. Preserve that correction instead of silently choosing one earlier proposal.

annotations.body: Intentional expressive exception: keep occasional glitch-like graphic interruptions as an option requested by the human. A generic anti-slop rule must not automatically remove this character. Agent proposal: avoid continuous distortion, text-reading disruption, or decoration on controls, because those would erase the quiet/graphic contrast. Trigger, duration, frequency, interruption behavior and reduced-motion/static treatment remain untested questions.
annotations.limitations: Marathon/trailer comparison is a human association. No specific clip was supplied or inspected. No numerical motion values, trigger, or approved recipe is inferred from static references.

decision.rationale: Preserve the requested character while distinguishing it from an always-on glitch treatment that the user did not ask for.

reference.title: Mixed rhythm - feedback synthesis
reference.creator: Agent synthesis; human quote stored in scoped annotation
reference.observations:
MIXED DIRECTION - AGENT SYNTHESIS OF HUMAN FEEDBACK

Human preference: combine quiet and graphic sections, rather than choose one style for the whole experience. Preserve quiet surroundings and an ending with space to breathe; allow graphic-heavy moments elsewhere.

Agent proposal: use Earthrise-like scale and negative space for quieter passages; Grand Tour-like layered graphic rhythm and strong type for selected sections. Occasional glitch-like interruptions can express contrast.

The user associates this rhythm with Marathon/trailers. No specific trailer or timestamps have been inspected. No timing, frequency, trigger, font or palette is settled.

Superseded framing: uniform A-only or B-only across the whole site. Keep A and B as useful ingredients, not bad styles.

Intentional exception: keep episodic glitch as a requested expressive option. Continuous distortion would erase the contrast; it is not the current interpretation.

Open: where should interruptions occur, and what static/reduced-motion alternative preserves the contrast? All implementation details remain proposals; no approval snapshot exists.
